findings.finding: The service admits P1..44095. Whole-core identity requires a valid whole-core runner contract; a mismatched contract fails before execution, rather than falling back to segmented Prefill.

Every actual panel, including a partial final panel, follows whole-core fill/core/drain/MLP. The whole-core layer branch ends in continue. The operator-panel and compatibility-segment paths below it are unreachable for a valid whole-core invocation.

All pinned FP8 fill/drain roles have K5120 or K6144. Their helper launches canonical-weight dequantization/CUTLASS with request workspace and returns its status. It never reaches the later Marlin compute branch for these shapes, including short/tail panels.
Startup nevertheless allocates and prepares all208 FP8 Marlin weights/scales under the current whole-core selection.

These assets remain live contract dependencies: inventory checks, launch guards and bound/matching receipts require Marlin pointers. They are compute-unused in the audited path, not yet safely removable under the existing contract.
NVFP4 Down still consumes its Marlin assets; those are outside the reclaim proposal. Legacy/projection-reset/parity/direct-runner paths retain their separate contracts.

The current M2..4 verifier has an existing AoSoA4-preswizzled consumer with one vector weight demand load and one next-block weight prefetch instead of four scalar loads/prefetches, plus no runtime XOR swizzle. Four-chain arithmetic and reductions are shared. Fewer instructions are not an established API gain.
